A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same research work, with matching methods and benchmark tables. Neither contains an appendix. However, v2 refers important experimental and implementation details to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF, limiting comparison of those details.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and rendering experiments on DTU and ShapeNet, qualitative real-world results, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and ablations and adds qualitative segmentation comparisons and physics simulations. The separately attributed Neuralangelo results do not affect this assessment.

M1.justification: The coupled superquadric–2D Gaussian representation, regularizers, adaptive block addition/pruning, and point-level refinement remain intact. Gaussian scale regularization already appears in v1. v2's example of using COLMAP point clouds for block addition does not establish that the implemented algorithm changed.

E1.justification: DTU, the same four ShapeNet categories, BlendedMVS, and self-captured scenes remain covered. v2 adds physics-simulation demonstrations involving throwing or dropping reconstructed parts (Figures 2 and 9), extending the application scenarios beyond editing and content generation.

E2.justification: v2 adds OmniSeg3D and Gaussian Grouping as qualitative comparators in Figure 6 and Neuralangelo's published results in Table 2. It also adds MonteBoxFinder to the ShapeNet comparison in Table 3, whereas v1 explicitly excluded it after reporting failures. These substantially broaden the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Retained stated settings agree, including 15 DTU scenes, 15 ShapeNet objects per category, 30k plus 30k training iterations, and the listed loss weights. However, v2 omits image resolutions, splits, baseline controls, and other settings, referring to unavailable supplementary material. Settings for the added comparisons are also insufficiently documented to establish protocol comparability.

E4.justification: The loss ablations, scale-regularization analysis, and both hyperparameter sweeps remain; v1 Tables VI and VII become v2 Table 6. v2 adds qualitative case comparisons examining segmentation artifacts against SAM-based methods. Figure 8 retains the primitive-count sensitivity question but drops one illustrated example.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Both primarily report averages across evaluated objects or scenes.

E6.justification: Results are substantially extended and revised. Table II/2 changes point-level DTU CD from 1.05 to 0.95 and time from approximately 50 to 40 minutes; 2DGS changes from 0.96 to 0.81 CD and 18 to 10 minutes. ShapeNet block-level rendering scores and several ablation entries also change; gun PSNR rises from 27.97 to 29.95, reversing its ranking against DBW's unchanged 28.72. New comparator results and simulation outcomes are added. These are reported updates, without established same-setting gains; v2's 0.95 also conflicts with the retained 1.05 in Tables 1 and 6.

T1.justification: v2 omits v1's explicit mathematical rendering formulation for projected covariance, Gaussian alpha weights, and composited RGB (Equations 5–7). The superquadric geometry, occupancy definitions, and optimization equations otherwise match after renumbering. No new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central claims of unsupervised part-aware reconstruction through a hybrid representation remain. v2 broadens the abstract's performance claim to real-life datasets and explicitly adds physical interactions to the stated contributions, extending the claimed applications.

C2.justification: v2 introduces an explanation of SAM-based methods' segmentation difficulties through indistinct textures, cross-view inconsistency, and feature misalignment. It omits v1's specific observation that limited views can produce point-level artifacts while block-level reconstructions remain smooth. The background-free-input limitation is retained.

D1.justification: Substantial reproducibility information present in v1 is absent from the supplied v2: rendering resolutions and splits, baseline point counts and adaptations, camera/mask processing, mesh extraction details, 100 Gaussians per face, scale c=0.15, threshold t=0.2, and 2048 samples per ray. v2 retains selected hyperparameters but directs readers to unavailable supplementary material. These are documentation omissions rather than established implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 removes the dedicated multi-view reconstruction overview and substantially refocuses positioning around mesh-based Gaussian splatting and SAM-based segmentation. It emphasizes simultaneous mesh/Gaussian optimization relative to previous mesh-binding approaches and adds references including Neuralangelo, Gaussian Grouping, OmniSeg3D, GARField, and Segment Any 3D Gaussians.

P1.justification: v2 introduces the PartGS name and extensively condenses and rewrites the narrative. It removes the standalone rendering exposition and multi-view related-work subsection, shortens experimental documentation, and combines the separate DTU and ShapeNet discussions into geometry and appearance evaluations.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is extensively reorganized. Separate DTU and ShapeNet figures are merged and reduced; real-world and application examples are condensed; physics and SAM-comparison panels are added; and two sensitivity tables become one. Table 1 gains a renderability column. The ablation figure adds highlights but reverses its with/without row labels relative to the caption and retained images.

improvement.justification: The added comparison methods, clearer research positioning, and physics demonstrations strengthen the paper's breadth. However, the supplied v2 loses substantial reproducibility detail and introduces conflicting DTU CD values and reversed ablation labels. Revised scores lack enough accompanying information to establish comparable improvements. With the referenced supplement unavailable, these benefits and harms do not support a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
